conclusion.saved_takeaway: TabM deliberately keeps only the first adapter randomized at initialization; other multiplicative factors start at1. Independent per-member losses and ensemble-aware validation are prior. Official paper code uses member-private output heads; current README recommends averaging class probabilities. Library bias rows share a copied initial bias.
conclusion.relationship_to_GNNM_and_extension: Direct factor-initialization and collective training baseline. Candidate is not an improved TabM port merely because intermediate factors are initialized differently.
conclusion.attributed_prior_vs_open_gap: Credit factor topology, first-adapter initialization, member losses, private-head option and validation-aware collective stopping. Proposed graph operation replaces random factor seeding with supervised graph residual directions under an identical warm function and descent safeguard.
conclusion.decisive_next_step: Use native probability pooling when reproducing TabM; disclose fixed raw-logit pool as a matched graph protocol choice. Include member-private and shared-head controls, native cold and warm controls, and full warm/gradient costs.

conclusion.relationship_to_GNNM_and_extension: Direct closest graph-supervised route initialization prior. Candidate must add something beyond GAT-to-SAGE parameter transfer.

conclusion.decisive_next_step: Source transfer/fusion boundary resolved. Use warm graph-supervised transfer as a close initialization control; do not claim all transferred experts preserve the warm GAT function.

conclusion.saved_takeaway: Link-MoE uses pair-specific softmax expert weights from separate MLP branches over structural heuristics and endpoint Hadamard features, then sigmoid of the weighted expert-score sum. conclusion.saved_takeaway: First fine-tune one target model, retain it as center, then train full models independently from its weights using cosine-cycle schedules. Pinned shared loop empties optimizer state by default and reloads first model weights; native reset differs from inherited warm Adam moments. More disagreement can accompany weaker members and worse OOD ensemble quality.
conclusion.relationship_to_GNNM_and_extension: Direct copied target-fine-tuned ensemble initialization ancestry. Native full-model rays differ from shared-W private-factor one-time graph-filtered CE-cotangent VJP expansion and its common-descent/functional/Armijo checks.
conclusion.attributed_prior_vs_open_gap: Attribute warm-copy branching and separation of target fine-tuning from diversification. The complete candidate operation can be a useful extension; held-out utility and originality remain unestablished. No exhaustive novelty claim.
conclusion.decisive_next_step: Add unchanged warm-copy GNNM continuation to a new prospective protocol amendment; optionally use warm untied copies as the quality reference for a broad copied-ensemble claim. Keep fixed raw-logit pool and equal tuning/cost accounting.
